name: violin-jabs-and-garden-party
style: Cinematic chamber suspense cue, voices talked and yelled rather than sung, raw broadcast-drama acting, working-class English crew: a ragged Somerset-burred woman, a flat-vowelled Bolton man, a gruff Cumbrian driver. Each yell punctuated by a single vicious sforzando violin jab with a hard gap of silence after it, a grinding low cello pedal tone beneath, rain-lashed siren, quick ECG pips. Midway the score flips to a prim tinkling harpsichord minuet with a dainty string quartet in triple time, distant as if leaking from a limousine; a fruity, port-soaked Home Counties aristocrat sneers through the glass. Ends abruptly on one unbroken ECG beep, nothing after
exclude: American accent, US twang, melodic vocal, rap, choir, pop, drum kit, groove, comedy, upbeat, synth, electric guitar, autotune, fade out, long intro, reverb wash
lyrics:
[Cold open: rain, siren, cello pedal growling, ECG pips racing]
[Yelled, Somerset woman, frantic]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[One violin jab]
[Yelled, Bolton man, out of breath]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[One violin jab]
[Roared, Cumbrian driver, at the windscreen]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[One violin jab, tyres skid, siren dies]
[Talked, Bolton man, baffled]
Why have we stopped?!
[Dainty harpsichord minuet with string quartet, faint, through car glass]
[Talked, fruity old aristocrat, muffled, sulking]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[Minuet snaps off, ECG pips slow]
[Barely audible, Somerset woman]
Fifty over twen—
[One unbroken ECG beep]
[Silence]
[End]
